data.plain: Counts, "current" states, live route totals, CI minimums, body-import minimums and readiness signals must say how they can be recomputed. If they cannot be recomputed, leave them out of lasting prose or mark them as snapshots with a date.

analogy.boundary: The board covers why a changing value needs a timestamp and a live source; a refresh time on its own does not mean the value is correct now.

maps.analogy: the departure time shown for a train
maps.doctrine: a live count or readiness signal

maps.analogy: the 'last updated' stamp on the board
maps.doctrine: the read time carried with the value

maps.analogy: the board's link to the live timetable feed
maps.doctrine: the route that recomputes it from its source

maps.analogy: treating a time painted on the wall as an old notice
maps.doctrine: marking an unsupported value as a dated snapshot

analogy.text: A train departure board shows when it last refreshed and updates from the live feed. A time painted on the wall stops being reliable as soon as the timetable changes.

reader.counterexample: A page states "47 components" as a flat fact, with no read time and no way to recount, and the number stays the same after more components are added.
reader.does_not_prove: A recompute route lets a reader check the value; it does not mean anyone has recomputed it since it was written.

example.text: The doctrine fact-claim audit checks that public fact rows state the expected count, point at the live code they were read from and cite only facts in the fixture graph, and it blocks a changing number that has no way to be recomputed.

reader.governs: When a live reading may appear in lasting text.
reader.plain: A number about something that keeps changing, like a current count or a readiness status, may sit in a lasting document only if it says when it was read and how to work it out again. Otherwise mark it as a dated snapshot.
reader.potential_misread: That a confident number in a document is current because it sounds definite, when what matters is whether there is a way to recount it.
reader.refuses: A frozen live count or 'current' state written as a fact with no read time and no way to recompute it.
reader.requires: The read time, the source and a recompute route for every live count or readiness signal, or a dated-snapshot label when any is missing.
reader.why_it_matters: A frozen 'current' number drifts away from reality as the thing it counts changes, and readers keep trusting the old reading.
